business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Export Distribution of High-Proof Traditional Sorghum Baijiu

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between the Government of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income, signed 1994, as amended by the 2019/2020 Protocol

Agreement between the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and the People's Republic of China on the Encouragement and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (signed 1979; additional protocol in place; still referenced by EU regulation on national investment treaties)
Agreement between the European Union and the People's Republic of China on the Protection and Enforcement of Intellectual Property Rights (effective 2022)
EU-China Geographical Indications Agreement (signed 2020, provisionally applied)
Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters (OECD, ratified by Luxembourg)
EU Anti-Money Laundering Directives and EU sanctions regulations directly applicable in Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 17 May 2013 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (AML/CFT Law), as amended; Law of 13 July 2017 establishing the beneficial ownership register (Register of Beneficial Owners, RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive); Law of 6 February 2023 adjusting the RBE access regime following ECJ rulings C-37/20 and C-601/20; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on central administration, internal governance and risk management, as amended; CSSF AML/CFT FAQ and Circulars applicable to non-bank professional lenders; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 January 2021 establishing the national risk assessment and identifying third-country high-risk jurisdictions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified notarized copy of the constitutive documents of each direct or indirect corporate shareholder up to the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary or competent registration authority in the country of origin of the shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or registry extract (in French, German, or English) for each corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or commercial court registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card copy of each ultimate beneficial owner and of each manager or authorized signatory, duly notarized or certified by the issuing authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office, police authority, or notary in the country of residence of the UBO/manager

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of address of the ultimate beneficial owner (utility bill, bank statement, or public registry certificate) dated not more than three months prior to submission
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, bank, or local public authority in the country of residence of the UBO

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Source-of-funds declaration and bank reference letter for each contribution to share capital, issued by an authorized credit institution or notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution in the country of origin of the contribution, or a notary in that jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn French or German translation of any document not drafted in Luxembourg's official administrative languages, performed and signed by a certified translator sworn before the Luxembourg District Court
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator admitted to the Luxembourg District Court

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg National Sanctions List, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists (Globally Authorised List), UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists, the U.S. OFAC SDN list, and the UK combined sanctions list, in accordance with Article 5-1 of the AML/CFT Law and CSSF expectations. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) are to be screened using a risk-based approach aligned with FATF Recommendation 12, including a minimum of enhanced due diligence for any PEP, close associates, and family members identified, with transaction monitoring and senior management approval required for high-risk PEPs. Screening is mandatory prior to incorporation and must be refreshed continuously or at least every six months, with documentary evidence preserved for at least five years post-closing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) via the Luxembourg Business Registers portal at www.lbr.lu (name clearance and reservation integrated in the RCS filing workflow; name availability can be searched electronically in the open RCS database)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be in French, German, or any language using the Latin alphabet; a mandatory transliteration into French, German, or English must be provided for names in non-Latin scripts; the name must be distinguishable from all other existing RCS names and must not contravene Luxembourg statutory naming rules under the Law of 19 December 2008 on the commercial register and company register, and the Law of 10 August 1915 as amended. The suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' is mandatory and must appear in the articles of association and all commercial documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within one month of receiving the official rejection notice issued by the Luxembourg Business Registers or the competent Commercial Registry office, the applicant or notary may file an administrative appeal with the Grand-Ducal Ministry of Justice via registered mail or through the LBR portal, supported by a letter of mandate and a legal memorandum demonstrating that the name satisfies Articles 1 to 3 of the Law of 19 December 2008 and is distinguishable from existing RCS entries. A motion for judicial review may thereafter be filed with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within three months of the ministerial decision. Notarized identifications and apostilled originals submitted with the rejection appeal remain valid for sixty days from the rejection date. An expedited re-submission of an amended name is available within five business days of rejection without paying a new reservation fee, subject to LBR practice and availability.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office alone is not permissible for a SARL engaging in physical export distribution of alcoholic beverages; the statutory seat must be a physical address in Luxembourg that is either owned or leased under a genuine contract, and must at minimum allow receipt of legal process and tax correspondence. A professional domiciliation service (société de domiciliation) is allowed under the Law of 31 May 1999 governing commercial agents, provided that the service includes a genuine physical presence and access to mail; pure remote virtual offices without physical floor space are not permissible.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspections: Low for a standard low-risk export distributor; estimated 5%–10% probability within the first three years, based on CSSF, the Company Registry, tax administration (ACD – Administration des Contributions Directes), and customs/excise authorities periodic substance checks. The risk increases to approximately 20%–30% if the registered office is shared with multiple unrelated companies or if the declared corporate purpose includes wholesale alcohol without supporting commercial substance documentation. A physical inspection may be performed by the Customs and Excise Administration (ADA) and the Food Safety Authority (ASTA) where alcoholic beverage distribution is involved.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name clearance and reservation fee (taxable service)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per LBR fee schedule for a reservation request (approximately EUR 40, converted at prevailing EUR/USD benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the electronic compendium of companies (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication fee calculated per page; typically EUR 120–140 for a standard SARL deed, at prevailing exchange rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (authentic act) including articles of association, appointment of management, and UBO declaration annex
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary officially appointed by the Ministry of Justice
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 February 2011 on notarial fees; standard SARL incorporation fee ranges EUR 1,500–2,200, plus disbursements

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial preparation of the UBO annex and submission of subsequent RBE filing to the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) statutory platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial service fee for UBO annex, typically EUR 100–200; RBE registration itself is free but notarial handling attracts standard fee; at prevailing exchange rate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague apostille and notarization bundle for corporate shareholder documents above the 25% threshold
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / competent apostille authority in each shareholder jurisdiction, and local notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Apostille tariffs per jurisdiction, commonly EUR 50–150 per document; notarization of passport copies and power of attorney under notarial fee schedule; bundled market benchmark USD 500–800

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn French/German translation of English or Chinese corporate and commercial documents (including articles of association of upstream entities, UBO due diligence files, powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted before the Luxembourg District Court
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Sworn translator statutory per-word or per-page tariff; typical fee for a cycle of 15–20 notarial pages is USD 750–1,100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees of Luxembourg counsel for pre-incorporation UBO piercing, AML/CFT procedure review, drafting of corporate authorizations, and compliance sign-off
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent Luxembourg law firm authorized under the Law of 10 August 1991 on the legal profession
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Luxembourg market benchmark, typically EUR 350–580 per hour; flat fee of USD 3,800–5,200 for Stage 1 standard SARL incorporating with up to two corporate layers and Chinese source-of-funds documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official certificate of registered office / domiciliation fee for a physical registered office (letter of authorization and proof of address)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Domiciliation service provider (société de domiciliation) regulated under the Law of 31 May 1999
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market annual domiciliation fee of EUR 650–900 for a standard physical registered-office arrangement with mail handling and secretarial support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Expedited handling and courier of apostilled originals from the People's Republic of China and Hong Kong SAR
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Courier service providers and apostille handling agents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: International document courier and apostille agent market benchmark; USD 250–350 for expedited China–Luxembourg cycle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Contingency reserve for additional certifications, ministerial permits for alcohol wholesale, and unforeseen due diligence scope expansion
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: General contingency allocated to counsel covering additional municipal licenses/official fees
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark safety margin equal to 5%–8% of total Stage 1 fixed fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as consolidated (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 et seq. as amended by the Law of 10 August 2016; business establishment licensing under the Law of 2 September 2011; excise regime for spirits under the Law of 21 December 2012.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); notarial execution before a Luxembourg notary public; beneficial-owner filing with the Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized acte constitutif (articles of incorporation and statutes) executed in French, registered with the RCS and published in the electronic Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (Mémorial C).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed and fully paid-up share capital is EUR 12,000 (Article 710-5). Cash contributions must be deposited, before notarization, into a blocked escrow account (compte de blocage) opened in the name of the company in formation with a Luxembourg credit institution; the bank issues an attestation de blocage released only upon presentation of the notarial deed. In-kind contributions require an independent report by an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [●] SARL

1. Share Subscription. The founder, acting as sole incorporator and sole shareholder, adopts the Company's articles of incorporation, approves the subscription of the entire share capital of EUR 12,000, and acknowledges that the share capital is fully paid up and held on a blocked account confirmed by the banker's attestation.

2. Registered Office. The Company shall maintain its registered office at the address stated in the articles of incorporation, within the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.

3. Officer Appointment. [Mr/Ms Given Family Name] is appointed manager (gérant) of the Company for an indefinite term, with sole power to bind the Company and to complete all RCS and business license filings.

4. Effectiveness. This resolution shall take effect immediately upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Pre-Incorporation KYC Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – eRCS online portal (www.lbr.lu); no formal name-reservation window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the eRCS portal and run a search to verify that the proposed corporate name, formatted as 'Company Name SARL', does not conflict with any existing registered entity, protected trademark, or confusingly similar designation. Simultaneously assemble the full KYC and identity documentation of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and proposed managers. Have foreign public documents legalized by apostille and translated into French or German by a sworn translator, and instruct the chosen Luxembourg notary to produce the first draft of the statutes.
required_dossiers: eRCS corporate name availability search report
Certified passport or national identity card copies of all shareholders
Proof of residential address and tax residence certificate of each shareholder
Bank and professional references for AML/KYC
Curriculum vitae and police clearance of proposed managers
Draft articles of incorporation (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry reports a name conflict, obtain a written consent from the prior titleholder or revise the proposed corporate name and repeat the search; the notary adjusts the draft statutes and reissues the documentation package.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the Escrow Capital Account and Obtaining the Banker's Blockage Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution or EU-authorized bank passporting into Luxembourg (Professional of the Financial Sector)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open, in the name of the company 'en formation', a dedicated blocked-capital Euro account with a Luxembourg credit institution. Instruct all shareholders to remit from their own external bank accounts the full subscribed capital, minimum EUR 12,000, or the higher amount stated in the draft statutes. Instruct the bank not to dispose of the funds until it receives the notarial acte constitutif, and obtain the banker's attestation de blocage (capital blockage certificate) dated no earlier than eight calendar days before the scheduled notarial execution.
required_dossiers: Account opening application for the company in formation
Draft incorporation deed with capital clause
Passport copies and KYC package of all signatories
Source of wealth and source of funds declarations
Bank reference letter from each remitting foreign bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises enhanced due diligence queries, promptly provide supplementary documentary evidence of the commercial purpose, the group structure, and the ultimate beneficial ownership chain. If the attestation is refused, dated improperly, or issued by an unapproved institution, obtain a corrected banker's certificate before notarization; otherwise the notary must postpone execution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Notarial Act of Incorporation (Acte Constitutif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (notaire) competent for the arrondissement where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver to the notary the final French-language statutes and the banker's blockage attestation. Hold a physical or lawfully permitted remote execution session in which all incorporators, or their duly appointed attorneys-in-fact, sign the acte constitutif before the notary. The notary verifies the legal capacity of the parties, the AML/KYC file, the capital blockage condition, and the legality of the corporate object, including the wholesale export of alcoholic beverages. Where a contribution in kind is made, annex the report of the réviseur d'entreprises agréé and attach the valuation. The notary issues one original and certified copies (expéditions) for the public records.
required_dossiers: Final French-language articles of incorporation (statuts)
Capital blockage attestation issued by the Luxembourg bank
Identity documents of all incorporators
Notarial power of attorney for any proxy signatory
Statutory auditor's report on in-kind contribution, if applicable
AML declarations and tax identification numbers of shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues observations or requisitions, cure the drafting deficiencies, initial any rectifications (paraphe), and reconvene the execution session before the original deadline. Payment of the 0.5% capital registration duty may be made at the notary's office, but late filing exposes the company to the applicable default surcharge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration, Capital Duty Payment and Publication in the Electronic Companies Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), e-RCS electronic filing window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within ten days after the notarial act, file through the notary, or a licensed agent, the application for registration (formulaire A) accompanied by the expédition of the acte constitutif using the eRCS portal. Pay the 0.5% registration duty on the subscribed capital (droit d'enregistrement) to the Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), and pay the statutory RCS filing fee. Upon admission, the LBR assigns the RCS registration number, certifies the registration, publishes the company particulars in the electronic Mémorial C, and the company acquires legal personality from the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Original expédition of the notarized act of incorporation
Formulaire A – official application for RCS registration
Proof of payment of the 0.5% capital registration duty
Banker's capital blockage attestation
Identity details, nationality, and residence of managers and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects or queries the filing, cure the identified inconsistencies and resubmit the corrected file within fifteen days of the notice. If the registry maintains a refusal, appeal to the tribunal d'arrondissement sitting in commercial matters. Re-filing after correction within the original month does not trigger additional capital duty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Beneficial Owner, Social Security and Business Establishment License Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE – Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs); Ministry of the Economy – Direction générale des Classes moyennes; Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax and municipal business tax with the ACD and for VAT with the AEDT. File the beneficial-owner declaration with the RBE within one month of RCS registration. Apply to the Ministry of the Economy for the statutory autorisation d'établissement covering wholesale distribution of beverages under ISIC 4632, and, given the excise nature of baijiu, register with the Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises) for the EMCS duty-suspension regime if bonded warehousing is used for export. Register the employer with the CCSS and complete the social security affiliation declarations for any employees.
required_dossiers: RCS certificate of registration and extract
Certified copy of the notarial incorporation deed
Business establishment permit application form (wholesale trade activity)
Criminal record certificate (bulletin n°3) of each manager
Lease agreement or registered-office agreement for the Luxembourg premises
RBE beneficial-owner declaration form
Excise/EMCS registration form for spirits if bonded storage is intended
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the autorisation d'établissement file is incomplete, remedy the deficiencies within the administrative deadline; an adverse decision may be challenged through a recours gracieux to the Minister of the Economy and thereafter by an appeal to the tribunal administratif. VAT registration is issued separately by the AEDT once the standard registration form is accepted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des Classes moyennes (Ministry of the Economy, Department for Middle Classes), Luxembourg; customs and excise supervision by the Administration des douanes et accises
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for wholesale trade in beverages, issued under the Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to craft, commercial, and industrial professions; supplemented by the excise authorization and EMCS registration for duty-suspended export of spirit drinks.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environment Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for wholesale distribution and sealed-bottle warehousing of baijiu: the activity is a de minimis class-4 (notification) operation under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 May 1999 on dangerous establishments. A prior environmental screening declaration and class-3 type authorization become mandatory only where covered warehouse floor area exceeds 10,000 m² or where bulk storage of flammable ethyl alcohol exceeds the thresholds of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment and its implementing grand-ducal regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with the Law of 19 December 2008 on water and municipal sanitary sewer discharge limits (pH 6.5–9.5, BOD5 ≤ 500 mg/L, COD ≤ 1000 mg/L) under the Administration de la gestion de l'eau; no significant VOC point-source emissions from sealed bottles, but any heating or ventilation equipment must comply with the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 16 October 1989 on atmospheric emissions; waste handling per the Law of 21 March 2012 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 8 June 2018; all excise movements of spirits are monitored through the EMCS system.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), including inspection of extinguishers, emergency exits, and compliant storage of flammable spirit containers; structural load clearance for warehouse racking certified by a licensed engineering office; and occupational workplace clearance issued by the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) confirming compliance with workplace health and safety rules under the Law of 17 June 1994 and implementing regulations; where six or more employees are engaged, an internal health-and-safety delegate structure must be established.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS), structural load inspection certificates for the warehousing and racking system issued by an independent engineering office, and an occupational workplace clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) covering emergency preparedness, first aid, ventilation, and ergonomics under the Labor Code; any premises storing spirits above the flammable-liquid threshold must also satisfy the fire-resistance standards set out in the amended Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 November 2011.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration, domains and VAT – and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS via the single portal Guichet.lu; direct tax registration with the Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned Luxembourg SARL, the statutory path is: (1) execute the articles of association before a Luxembourg notary and fully subscribe/share up capital; (2) file the incorporation file with the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS/Guichet.lu); the RCS registration automatically allocates the national business number (numéro d'identification) and records the entity for corporate tax purposes with the ACD; (3) file Form 1000 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) with the AEDT through the 'MyGuichet' e-desk together with the RCS extract, registered office proof, director and shareholder identification, and banking details; (4) obtain the Luxembourg VAT identification number (numéro de TVA LU...) before issuing invoices; (5) obtain an EU EORI number from customs for export declarations and, for alcohol, arrange excise duty suspension/authorised warehouse status or periodic excise reporting under the national alcohol excise system; (6) submit Intrastat/ECS declarations once goods are dispatched.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box system exists; SARL is classified by law as an opaque, taxable entity fully resident in Luxembourg. Relevant elections available: (a) VAT group election (assujetti unique) for financially integrated entities; (b) small-business VAT exemption election (franchise en base) where annual turnover is at or below EUR 35,000; (c) domestic fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) for 95%-plus group shareholdings for CIT/net wealth tax; (d) hybrid-mismatch structuring must be assessed under ATAD implementation, but no generic entity classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For non-established foreign suppliers, any taxable supply performed in Luxembourg triggers a Luxembourg VAT registration obligation without a de minimis turnover threshold. For a Luxembourg-established SARL, the domestic small-business exemption (no VAT charge) applies only when annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 (excluding VAT), but a registered export wholesaler will typically be required to register because turnover exceeds that threshold or because supplies are not eligible for the small business exemption; the actual registration threshold is therefore effectively EUR 0 for export-oriented activity requiring VAT identification and zero-rating.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently impose a real-time CT (continuous tax control) clearance system, invoice API clearance, or digital stamping for private B2B invoices. Commercial invoices must comply with the EU invoicing rules and contain the Luxembourg VAT number and the statement of zero-rating. E-invoicing is mandatory only in the B2G segment, where a PEPPOL BIS 3.0 e-invoice must be channelled through a certified PEPPOL access point. Export procedures require electronic filing of the Standard Export Declaration via the Customs ECS/PLDA portal, with no separate tax-chapter API requirement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A supply of Chinese baijiu qualifies for the 0% VAT export exemption if the goods are physically dispatched or transported outside the European Union by the supplier or for the supplier's account, as provided by Article 146(1)(a) of the EU VAT Directive. The SARL must hold VAT registration in Luxembourg, issue an invoice referring to the exemption, and prove through transport/customs evidence that the goods left EU territory. Export to other EU Member States qualifies for intra-Community supply exemption instead of export zero-rating, subject to the buyer's valid EU VAT number, not the export 0% rule.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'Exportation) filed via the Luxembourg ECS/PLDA customs connection
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note demonstrating exit from the EU
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent proof of export proceeds receipt (SWIFT MT103, bank confirmation, or authenticated letter of credit payment settlement)
Commercial invoice with the 0% VAT reference and buyer/vendor VAT/EORI numbers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: A VAT audit will reassess the export as a standard-rated Luxembourg supply if the 0% deduction is not substantially supported within the statutory records; the resulting VAT, late-payment interest and default surcharges are collected from the supplier. In cases of false or fraudulent zero-rating, the AEDT may apply penalties of up to 100% of the tax evaded and the limitation period is extended in fraud cases; criminal tax fraud can also attract fines and imprisonment. Input VAT attributed to export sales is refundable only after documentary verification, and an export refund claim may be clawed back with penalty if the documents are not retained for at least 5 years or the exporter stages a sham export/round-tripping transaction.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance exercises policy oversight, while the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises credit institutions, e-money institutions, and payment services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible. Luxembourg applies the EU Treaty freedoms under Article 63 TFEU and maintains no general exchange-control approvals for current account or capital account operations. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are subject only to corporate-law formalities, domestic withholding tax at 15% where applicable, and applicable treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief. Foreign-currency accounts are freely permitted, and conversion may be executed through any CSSF-regulated credit institution without prior central-bank authorization. Practical constraints are limited to AML/KYC verification, CSSF conduct-of-business reporting, and BCL balance-of-payments statistics filings.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements and no mandatory conversion ratios in Luxembourg. Export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or freely converted into EUR. For external trade and balance-of-payments statistics, banks submit underlying transaction-purpose coding to the BCL. An exporting SARL must retain shipping documents, customs declarations, invoices, and payment records sufficient to support such reporting instruments. No central-bank approval is required for retention, repatriation, or conversion of export earnings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account
Operational Account and Cross-Border Credit Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Medium for EU/EEA-authorized e-money institutions or payment service providers licensed by the CSSF or passporting under the EU Payment Services Directive 2 (PSD2). Rating: Low for offshore, non-EEA digital EMIs that do not maintain an EU establishment or passport. The SARL may use a regulated EMI for transaction collections and routine supplier disbursements, but an EMI cannot issue or confirm commercial letters of credit, and full trade-finance documentation requires a licensed credit institution. Legal constraints under Luxembourg PSD2 transposition include client-money safeguarding rules, CSSF due-diligence duties, and prohibition against deposit-taking; principal treasury balances should remain with a credit institution and, where possible, benefit from the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For corporate onboarding, Luxembourg law and CSSF AML/CFT regulations require reliable identification of directors and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, at least one authorised manager or director must attend a physical interview, or a bank-approved video-verification interview where the institution expressly permits digital onboarding; fully remote account opening is generally unavailable for entities engaged in operational trade finance. Non-EU resident directors or shareholders may be verified through apostilled or legalised passport copies, corporate-registry extracts, banker’s references, and sworn affidavits. The CSSF expects the bank to establish a demonstrable personal link to the ultimate beneficial owner, so a physical interview is strongly recommended to avoid automatic escalation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First-time corporate customer with a beneficial owner resident in a third jurisdiction, e.g., PRC or Hong Kong, and no established EU economic footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registry extract and Articles of Association of the Luxembourg SARL; group structure chart; certified and apostilled passport copies; power of attorney; sworn source-of-funds letter; shareholder loan agreement; AML beneficial-ownership declaration; notarised and legalised corporate documents; and bank references from the incorporating jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-flow complexity involving high-proof alcoholic-beverage exports and cross-border invoicing creating elevated excise-evasion or trade-based money-laundering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete trade-file comprising contractual agreements, pro-forma and commercial invoices, packing lists, customs SAD/export declarations, excise movement certificates under EMCS, bills of lading or cargo manifests, cargo insurance policies, liquor import or wholesale licences, certificates of origin, and pre-shipment inspection reports.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request for high-value FX conversions and rapid outbound payments to suppliers and distributors before the bank has an established transaction history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution approving payment and FX-conversion limits; detailed payment schedule; counterparty bank details and trade-registry proof; underlying order confirmations; irrevocable letter-of-credit drafts where applicable; sanctions-screening outputs maintained by the bank; and a signed annual compliance attestation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital-escrow-account funding derived from shareholder loans or third-party financing while the exporting SARL has no operating track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the contributing shareholder; source-of-wealth memorandum; supporting bank statements for the remitted funds; notarised loan or subscription agreements; corporate approvals at shareholder level; and a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming absence of bearer shares and full beneficial-ownership transparency.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions should be remitted by SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, or MT202 for the interbank leg, using full remitter details and an ECB/BCL balance-of-payments purpose code reflecting equity transactions or direct-investment equity capital. Shareholder loans should be coded as intercompany financing or loans related to direct investment, with the loan agreement referenced in the remittance information. Funds should be routed to the SARL’s euro account at BIL, BCEE, or Société Générale Luxembourg. Before transfer, the bank must receive the board resolution, subscription agreement, updated share-register extract, and complete KYC pack to prevent AML-related suspension. If the contribution is denominated in CNY or USD, conversion to EUR should be carried out through the bank’s FX dealing desk using a spot transaction, or a forward if the inflow timing is uncertain. The capital-escrow account must not be debited for operational expenses without corporate approvals and a clear treasury mandate.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro payments to counterparties inside the SEPA/EEA zone, the exporter should use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer. For non-SEPA euro payments or foreign-currency settlements to Chinese or global distributors, SWIFT MT103 messages must include the correct BOP purpose code for goods-wholesale transactions. For high-value, high-risk or Chinese-origin liquor cargo, the preferred clearing rail is a commercial letter of credit confirmed by a Luxembourg bank and governed by the UCP 600 rules. LC settlements require presentation of the commercial invoice, complete bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, health or phytosanitary certificates, and Chinese export or baijiu-specific approvals. Open-account disbursements against MT103 may be used after established trade history, subject to invoice validation and supply-chain evidence. Trade-finance facilities may support sight or usance LC discounting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/CNH deliverable FX forwards entered with a CSSF-regulated credit institution or through an ISDA/FIA master agreement, with tenor matched to the underlying export settlement schedule.

Non-deliverable forwards on CNY/USD or CNY/EUR for onshore RMB exposure where the overseas supplier cannot deliver offshore CNY; settled in EUR or USD at maturity and documented as risk-reducing under EU EMIR reporting.
FX swaps and tom-next swaps used to manage rollovers of export proceeds and temporary working-capital funding mismatches in EUR, CNY, and USD.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps converting long-dated CNY or USD exposure into EUR to hedge currency mismatch on shareholder loans and long-term trade receivables.
Plain-vanilla EUR/CNY and EUR/USD over-the-counter option structures, limited to purchased puts and calls with approved premium budgets under the board treasury policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited (if applicable) annual accounts comprising balance sheet, profit-and-loss statement and notes, approved by shareholders and deposited with the commercial register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Trade and Companies Register (RCS).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after each financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing leads to formal LBR warning, a commercial court injunction with successive coercive fines, and continued non-compliance ultimately allows administrative strike-off of the SARL from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 100) covering corporation tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, including shareholding changes and export-related transfer pricing documentation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, standard deadline is 31 December of the year following the reporting year, unless the tax filing notice states an earlier date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late return triggers monthly default interest (0.6%-0.8%), administrative fines under the LIR, ACD unilateral assessment, and loss of technical reserves or filing benefits until the return is submitted.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT settlement and EU recapitulative customer statement covering export/zero-rated sales of baijiu and all intra-community supplies; proof of export must be retained and reported.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly periodic returns are due by the 30th after the tax period; if annual filing is authorised, the annual form is due by 31 March of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or late payment yields statutory late interest, administrative penalties and, for deliberate omission, criminal sanctions; failure to substantiate export also jeopardises zero-rated status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial owner declaration update to the UBO / RBE register on share transfers or changes in control, together with documented annual review of beneficial-ownership records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days from the share transfer or control change; where no change occurs, no statutory filing deadline applies, but annual internal verification must be performed and evidence kept.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or inaccurate filing exposes the SARL and responsible managers to administrative fines and criminal penalties under the RBE law; persistent non-compliance may trigger investigation and enforcement by public prosecutors.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit is mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of three thresholds: balance-sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, and average number of employees exceeding 50. Mandatory also for public-interest entities and consolidated supervision cases.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 and the Commercial Code; EU-adopted IFRS is permitted for consolidated annual accounts and, under specific options, for individual annual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO re-filing is imposed in Luxembourg. The SARL must, upon each shareholding transfer or other control change, verify the effective shareholder and file an updated declaration with the RBE within 30 days. Management must annually re-check the accuracy of the internal share register, minutes and RBE filing and remedy any identified discrepancy without delay.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members and Share Transfers
Minute Book of Shareholders' Meetings and Director Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,000 - 5,500 per year for a Luxembourg SARL registered office and corporate agent/domiciliation provider.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 8,000 - 25,000 per year for a certified Luxembourg statutory audit when audit thresholds are exceeded.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% corporate income tax (IRC); plus 7% solidarity surcharge on the IRC, resulting in a headline net rate of 18.19%; municipal business tax (IBP) of approximately 6.75% applies in Luxembourg City, yielding a combined effective headline rate of approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays. Available incentives include an 80% exemption for qualifying IP income under the IP box regime, a 20% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure, the notional interest deduction (NID) on new equity, and an investment tax credit for digitisation and environmental assets. For a standard trading and wholesale company, the effective tax rate remains the combined statutory rate of approximately 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no time limit in Luxembourg; carryback is prohibited; anti-abuse rules may restrict monetisation in cases of cessation or major ownership change)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed electronically via the MyGuichet.lu portal or in paper form with the Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due by 30 April of the calendar year following the tax year for calendar-year taxpayers; the director of the ACD may grant a filing extension upon written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: Luxembourg trade register number, legal form (SARL), registered office address, and VAT identification number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg SARL identification data; provide the ultimate shareholder's name, country of residence, and consolidated group structure in the annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: statutory reporting period and confirmation of accounts closing date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate a fiscal year-end corresponding to the commercial accounting period; ensure the period does not exceed 12 months unless properly justified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of commercial profit: accounting profit before tax derived from balance sheet and P&L accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report full worldwide taxable profit if the SARL is tax resident in Luxembourg; if a permanent establishment exists in another State, allocate profits under the applicable DTA and Luxembourg apportionment rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable profit: non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back fines, excessive director remuneration, and 50% of certain hospitality costs; deduct 100% of qualifying participation-exemption dividends and 80% of IP box income. Corrections from transfer pricing audits must be added if a controlled transaction is at non-arm's-length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base: taxable amount after loss carryforwards and exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply statutory loss carryforwards without time limitation, but observe annual offset restrictions applicable under minimum taxation and anti-abuse provisions for loss-borrowing entities.

Compute 17% IRC on the taxable base; add 7% solidarity surcharge (i.e., 1.19 percentage points); then calculate municipal business tax (IBP) separately using the local rate for the municipality of the registered office.

Report any Luxembourg corporate income tax prepayments and withholding tax credits; foreign tax credits and domestic tax credits for eligible IP income or notional interest deduction must be substantiated with documentation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of up to EUR 250 per return; if not filed after a reminder, additional fines may be imposed. Late payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month on unpaid tax (7.2% per year). In cases of wilful or bad-faith non-filing, the tax debt may be increased by up to 100% and criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 may apply.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on outbound dividend distributions; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the corporate parent holds at least 10% of the share capital and the holding period is at least 12 months. Under the China-Luxembourg DTA, a reduced rate generally of 5% may apply for a corporate beneficial owner holding at least 10% of the capital, provided substance and beneficial-ownership conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must hold a valid Luxembourg tax residency certificate (Form 300) from the ACD and submit it, with a risk-analysis form, to the paying agent. The payer applies the reduced rate at source or applies for tax benefit relief through Form 101 (withholding tax exemption request). If withholding tax has been over-deduction at source, a refund claim must be filed with the ACD within the statutory period, generally within one year from the end of the calendar year of the dividend payment; annual documentation must evidence that the shareholder is the beneficial owner and has not used the Luxembourg entity as a letterbox.

cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Statutory rate for royalties and interest is 0% under Luxembourg domestic law; no withholding tax is generally imposed on payments of arm's-length interest and royalties to non-residents. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive can further secure an exemption where linked enterprises are established in the EU and meet the 25% shareholding test. Anti-abuse rules deny relief if the transaction is not justified by valid economic substance.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (consolidated annual group turnover threshold triggering the obligation to prepare and maintain a Master File and Local File; these files must be submitted to the ACD within 30-45 days upon request).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations; however, the tax administration enforces a substance doctrine under anti-BEPS, ATAD, and treaty case law. Strong economic substance (own office, full-time local staff, local board documentation and management decisions in Luxembourg, adequate equity, and genuine operational risk) is mandatory to secure Luxembourg tax residence, treaty benefits, parent-subsidiary relief, and IP box advantages. A deficient substance profile raises a rebuttable presumption of abuse of law and may lead to recharacterisation of income, denial of treaty relief, and exit taxation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate submission of false declarations, omission of export turnover, use of concealed foreign bank accounts, fabrication of intercompany invoices, or commission of sham transactions to reduce Luxembourg corporate income tax and withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recoverable tax plus late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; administrative increase of up to 100% of the tax evaded in cases of bad faith; criminal fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to five years for responsible individuals. The competent Luxembourg prosecutor may additionally seize goods used in the smuggling or export of alcohol.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts and penalties where they have personally directed fraudulent arrangements; courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution of the evaded amounts, issue travel bans, and impose custodial sentences of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SARL as a formal entity with no real economic activity and no local substance, while all sales, management, and negotiation of Chinese baijiu export contracts are carried out by the parent abroad; claiming directive or treaty relief without commercial justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Loss of treaty and EU directive benefits; recharacterisation as hidden dividend distribution and assessment of 15% dividend withholding tax; additional penalties under abus de droit (abuse of law) equal to a maximum of 30% of the tax evaded; the entity may be deemed a tax avoidance vehicle with immediate tax recovery from the parent in the form of deemed exit gains.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors risk personal liability if they signed management statements certifying substance that does not exist; civil restitution may cover the entire tax not withheld; travel restrictions and disqualification of directors may be imposed; in cases of international money laundering or sham activity, imprisonment up to 5 years may follow.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving cash payments from distributors without applying customer due diligence, failing to report suspicious transactions to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), operating a high-proof spirits export operation with sanctioned parties, or facilitating the laundering of proceeds generated from illegal operations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties of up to EUR 1,000,000 or 10% of the annual turnover for administrative violation of the AML law; criminal penalties for laundering offences (up to 5 years imprisonment and/or fines up to EUR 500,000); revocation of the alcohol wholesale licence and prohibition from holding certain commercial functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and AML compliance officers are personally liable for criminal fines in their supervisory capacity; civil liability for restitution of laundered funds and legal costs may attach directly to their personal assets; the power to impose travel bans and temporary serving of commercial prohibition orders further exposes them to administrative revocation of passport rights where a serious laundering scheme is proven.
